I completed the implementation of block and txs announcements (though we aren't taking txs), such that we don't announce an object to a peer who has announced to us. This uses a small per-channel cache of hashes, configurable size. That required a `node::channel`, derived from `network::channel` so that tx/block state can be hung off of the channel without hacking it back into the network lib.

This uses a simple circular buffer of hashes. That can later be optimized using a circular cuckoo filter, reducing storage space and maybe search time. But it's trivial already, so no big deal.

elements.text: Spent the day today implementing pruning of the prevouts cache. When the node becomes current it starts announcing blocks. The announcement is handled by the snapshot chaser and determines if the top candidate is also confirmed, at which point the prevout table can be purged - since all blocks that have been validated are also confirmed. The table purge work was previously complete, just had to integrate it. This reclaims over 22GB on validated runs. The operation takes about 50 ms.

elements.text:
This is looking really good Rowan.

I think it would be worth splitting the header events into their own plots, since these are so rapid initially, and so infrequent later, that they get completely buried the block plots.

Also, it might be interesting to see downloaded and validated blocks in the pie chart. Downloaded will always be <= to validated which is always <= confirmed. But unlike confirmed, these are not sequential. You would have to maintain a count. That would be fine unless the node is restarted with partial completions of download/validate, since you wouldn't have an accurate count. But it's also the case that a validated block implies that all blocks up to that height are downloaded, and a confirmed block implies all blocks up to that point are validated. So you could correct quickly.
